easy.question: Who spoke to Moses in the first verse?
answers: Pharaoh
The Lord
Aaron
easy.explanation: The verse says explicitly, “And the Lord spoke unto Moses.”

easy.question: What did the Lord command regarding every firstborn?
answers: To set it apart as holy
To hide it
To sell it
easy.explanation: The command is, “Sanctify unto me all the firstborn.”

easy.question: Which beings are included in this command?
answers: Only human beings
Only animals
Human beings and animals
easy.explanation: The verse includes “both of man and of beast.”

medium.question: What can we understand from the fact that the command comes after the Lord spoke to Moses?
answers: The command was given to Moses by the Lord
Moses invented the command
The people requested the command
medium.explanation: The verse first says that the Lord spoke to Moses and then gives the command.

medium.question: According to the verse, what does “whatever openeth the womb” describe?
answers: Something that closes the womb
The first offspring to come from the womb
The last child to be born
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the first offspring born from its mother.

medium.question: How does the verse connect “firstborn” with “whatever openeth the womb”?
answers: It refers to the first offspring to come from the womb
It refers only to male children
It refers to every child in a family
medium.explanation: The verse defines the firstborn as the one that first opens the womb.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “it is mine” emphasize?
answers: That the firstborn belongs to the Lord and is dedicated to him
That the firstborn belongs only to the family
That the firstborn has no obligations
challenge.explanation: “It is mine” emphasizes that the firstborn belongs to the Lord and must be set apart.

challenge.question: What exact condition is implied by “whatever openeth the womb”?
answers: That the offspring is the oldest by age
That the offspring is the first to come from its mother’s womb
That the offspring is the only child in the family
challenge.explanation: The phrase focuses on the first offspring to emerge from the womb.

challenge.question: According to the wording of the verse, to whom does the command directly apply?
answers: To all nations and all creatures
Only to Israelite priests
To the children of Israel, both humans and animals
challenge.explanation: The command is specifically given concerning the children of Israel, including both people and animals.

That the firstborn belongs only to the family
That the firstborn has no obligations

That the offspring is the only child in the family
questions.explanation: The phrase focuses on the first offspring to emerge from the womb.

answers: To all nations and all creatures
Only to Israelite priests
To the children of Israel, both humans and animals
questions.explanation: The command is specifically given concerning the children of Israel, including both people and animals.

easy.question: From where did the children of Israel come out?
answers: Egypt
Canaan
Babylon
easy.explanation: The verse says, “when ye came out from Egypt.”

easy.question: In which month did the Israelites leave Egypt?
answers: The month of Tishri
The month of Abib
The month of Kislev
easy.explanation: The verse says they came out “in the month Abib.”

easy.question: What must not be eaten according to the verse?
answers: Honey
Milk
Leavened bread
easy.explanation: The verse says, “there shall no leavened bread be eaten.”

medium.question: Why were Moses and the people commanded to remember the day they left Egypt?
answers: Because the Lord brought them out by strength of hand
Because they found a land flowing with milk and honey there
Because they began serving the Lord in Canaan
medium.explanation: They were to remember that the Lord brought them out “by strength of hand.”

medium.question: In the phrase “there shall no leavened bread be eaten,” what is meant by “leavened bread”?
answers: Meat roasted over a fire
Bread or another food that has risen
A sweet fruit such as honey
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to food made with leaven, especially risen bread.

medium.question: What is the order of events described in these verses?
answers: Entering the land, leaving Egypt, and eating leavened bread
Eating leavened bread, entering the land, and leaving Egypt
Leaving Egypt, entering the land, and serving the Lord in that month
medium.explanation: The verses describe leaving Egypt, later entering the land, and then keeping this service in that month.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “house of bondage” reveal about Egypt?
answers: Egypt was the place where the Israelites were enslaved
Egypt was a large royal palace
Egypt was a land where people worked only in farming
challenge.explanation: “House of bondage” emphasizes that Egypt was the place of Israel’s slavery.

challenge.question: What does “a land flowing with milk and honey” emphasize about the Promised Land?
answers: That it was full of houses of bondage
That it was rich and fertile
That it was located inside Egypt
challenge.explanation: The phrase describes a land blessed with abundance and good conditions for living.

challenge.question: When were the Israelites to keep “this service”?
answers: Only before leaving Egypt
Only after reaching another land
When the Lord brought them into the land he swore to give their ancestors
challenge.explanation: The command follows the words, “when the Lord shall bring thee into the land.”

answers: Egypt was the place where the Israelites were enslaved

Egypt was a land where people worked only in farming
questions.explanation: “House of bondage” emphasizes that Egypt was the place of Israel’s slavery.

questions.question: What does “a land flowing with milk and honey” emphasize about the Promised Land?
answers: That it was full of houses of bondage
That it was rich and fertile
That it was located inside Egypt
questions.explanation: The phrase describes a land blessed with abundance and good conditions for living.

answers: Only before leaving Egypt

questions.explanation: The command follows the words, “when the Lord shall bring thee into the land.”

paragraphs.title: The Feast of Unleavened Bread and Its Story

easy.question: How many days were the Israelites to eat unleavened bread?
answers: Seven days
Three days
Fourteen days
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Seven days thou shalt eat unleavened bread.”

easy.question: What was the seventh day?
answers: A day of fasting
A feast to the Lord
A day of work
easy.explanation: The verse says, “in the seventh day shall be a feast to the Lord.”

easy.question: To whom were they to tell the story of the Exodus?
answers: The king
The priest
Their son
easy.explanation: The verse says, “thou shalt shew thy son.”

medium.question: What was not to be seen anywhere in the land during the seven days?
answers: Leavened bread and leaven
Unleavened bread and bitter herbs
Meat and fish
medium.explanation: The verse says that neither leavened bread nor leaven was to be seen in all their quarters.

medium.question: In the phrase “keep this ordinance in his season,” what does “in his season” mean?
answers: In secret
At its appointed time
Quickly
medium.explanation: The phrase means that the ordinance was to be observed at its appointed time.

medium.question: What is the connection between the sign on the hand and the Lord’s law in the mouth?
answers: The sign was meant to help keep the Lord’s law in a person’s mouth
The sign was meant to replace the law
The sign was meant to teach military skills
medium.explanation: The verse says the sign and memorial were intended so that the Lord’s law would be in their mouths.

challenge.question: In the sequence of these verses, what does “because of that” refer to?
answers: The commands to eat unleavened bread and avoid leaven
Building the tabernacle
Making Moses king
challenge.explanation: The phrase follows the commands about unleavened bread and leaven and points back to the Exodus.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the words “in all thy quarters”?
answers: The prohibition applied only inside the house
The prohibition applied throughout the person’s entire territory
The prohibition applied only in the Temple
challenge.explanation: The phrase extends the prohibition beyond the house to every part of their territory.

challenge.question: What does “from year to year” mean at the end of the passage?
answers: Only once
Every day anew
Every year, at the appointed time
challenge.explanation: The phrase indicates that the ordinance was to be observed annually.

questions.question: In the sequence of these verses, what does “because of that” refer to?
answers: The commands to eat unleavened bread and avoid leaven
Building the tabernacle
Making Moses king
questions.explanation: The phrase follows the commands about unleavened bread and leaven and points back to the Exodus.

questions.question: What can we infer from the words “in all thy quarters”?
answers: The prohibition applied only inside the house
The prohibition applied throughout the person’s entire territory
The prohibition applied only in the Temple
questions.explanation: The phrase extends the prohibition beyond the house to every part of their territory.

questions.question: What does “from year to year” mean at the end of the passage?
answers: Only once
Every day anew
Every year, at the appointed time
questions.explanation: The phrase indicates that the ordinance was to be observed annually.

easy.question: To which land would the Lord bring the Israelites?
answers: The land of Canaan
The land of Egypt
The land of Edom
easy.explanation: The verse says the Lord would bring them into the land of the Canaanites, meaning Canaan.

easy.question: With what was the firstborn of a donkey to be redeemed?
answers: Money
A lamb
A bull
easy.explanation: The verse says, “every firstling of an ass thou shalt redeem with a lamb.”

easy.question: What was the father to explain when his son asked, “What is this?”
answers: How the tabernacle was built
How they reached Canaan
That the Lord brought Israel out of Egypt by strength of hand
easy.explanation: The father was to explain that the Lord brought them out of Egypt, the house of bondage, by strength of hand.

medium.question: Why were the firstborn of humans and animals to be redeemed?
answers: To remember that the Lord spared Israel’s firstborn in the plague of the firstborn
To celebrate entering the land
To increase the family’s wealth
medium.explanation: The command is connected with the plague in which the Lord struck Egypt’s firstborn but spared Israel.

medium.question: In the phrase “all the firstborn of man among thy children shalt thou redeem,” what does “redeem” mean?
answers: Appoint him king
Release him through a payment or substitute
Send him to Egypt
medium.explanation: To redeem means to release through a redemption payment or substitute; the firstborn was not to be sacrificed.

medium.question: What is the order of events described in these verses?
answers: The son asks, Pharaoh sends Israel away, and the Lord brings them to Egypt
Israel dedicates the firstborn, the firstborn are born, and Pharaoh is released
The Lord brings Israel into the land, commands concerning the firstborn are given, and the father explains that the Lord brought them from Egypt
medium.explanation: The passage first describes entering the land and the command concerning the firstborn, then explains what the father should tell his son.

challenge.question: Why was this command to be “a token upon thine hand, and for frontlets between thine eyes”?
answers: To remember that the Lord brought Israel out of Egypt by strength of hand
To mark which child was born first
To remember the names of the kings of Canaan
challenge.explanation: The sign was meant to remind them of the Exodus and the Lord’s power.

challenge.question: What was special about the rule for the firstborn of a donkey?
answers: It did not need to be redeemed
It was redeemed with a lamb, and if not redeemed its neck was broken
The firstborn human was sacrificed in its place
challenge.explanation: The verse says that a donkey was redeemed with a lamb; otherwise its neck was to be broken, while human firstborn were redeemed.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the father’s command to explain this to his son in the future?
answers: The command was only for the generation that left Egypt
Children did not need to know its meaning
The memory of the Exodus was to be passed from generation to generation
challenge.explanation: The instruction shows that the story and meaning of the command were to continue through later generations.

questions.question: Why was this command to be “a token upon thine hand, and for frontlets between thine eyes”?
answers: To remember that the Lord brought Israel out of Egypt by strength of hand
To mark which child was born first
To remember the names of the kings of Canaan
questions.explanation: The sign was meant to remind them of the Exodus and the Lord’s power.

answers: It did not need to be redeemed

The firstborn human was sacrificed in its place
questions.explanation: The verse says that a donkey was redeemed with a lamb; otherwise its neck was to be broken, while human firstborn were redeemed.

answers: The command was only for the generation that left Egypt
Children did not need to know its meaning
The memory of the Exodus was to be passed from generation to generation
questions.explanation: The instruction shows that the story and meaning of the command were to continue through later generations.

easy.question: Why did God not lead the Israelites by the way of the land of the Philistines?
answers: So they would not see war and return to Egypt
Because the road was blocked
Because they had no food
easy.explanation: God feared that seeing war would make the people turn back to Egypt.

easy.question: By which route did God lead the Israelites?
answers: The way of the land of the Philistines
The way of the wilderness of the Red Sea
The way of Jerusalem
easy.explanation: The verse says that God led them through the way of the wilderness of the Red Sea.

easy.question: Who sent the Israelites out of Egypt?
answers: Moses
The king of the Philistines
Pharaoh
easy.explanation: The verse speaks of the time when Pharaoh let the people go.

medium.question: What might have happened if the Israelites had seen war?
answers: They would have settled in Philistia
They would have returned to Egypt
They would have gone immediately to the Red Sea
medium.explanation: God feared that war would make the people regret leaving and return to Egypt.

medium.question: In the phrase “Lest peradventure the people repent,” what does “lest peradventure” express?
answers: A fear that something might happen
An immediate action
Certainty
medium.explanation: The phrase expresses concern that the people might change their minds and return to Egypt.

medium.question: What happened after God did not lead the people by the way of the Philistines?
answers: God led them through the way of the wilderness of the Red Sea
Pharaoh brought them back to Egypt
The Israelites entered Canaan
medium.explanation: Instead of the nearby route, God led them through the wilderness toward the Red Sea.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the fact that the way of the Philistines was near, yet God did not choose it?
answers: The people’s readiness mattered more than simply taking the shortest route
The Israelites did not know the way
Philistia was very far away
challenge.explanation: Although the route was near, God avoided it because the people might become frightened by war.

challenge.question: What does the verse’s description of the Israelites as “harnessed” suggest?
answers: They left without any supplies
They left armed or equipped
They left alone in the wilderness
challenge.explanation: “Harnessed” suggests that they departed prepared or equipped, possibly armed.

challenge.question: What does the statement “God led the people about” mean?
answers: The people chose another route themselves
The people immediately returned to Egypt
God changed their route and led them by another path
challenge.explanation: The verse says that God directed the people away from the nearby route and through the wilderness.

questions.question: What can we infer from the fact that the way of the Philistines was near, yet God did not choose it?
answers: The people’s readiness mattered more than simply taking the shortest route
The Israelites did not know the way
Philistia was very far away
questions.explanation: Although the route was near, God avoided it because the people might become frightened by war.

questions.question: What does the verse’s description of the Israelites as “harnessed” suggest?
answers: They left without any supplies
They left armed or equipped
They left alone in the wilderness
questions.explanation: “Harnessed” suggests that they departed prepared or equipped, possibly armed.

questions.question: What does the statement “God led the people about” mean?
answers: The people chose another route themselves
The people immediately returned to Egypt
God changed their route and led them by another path
questions.explanation: The verse says that God directed the people away from the nearby route and through the wilderness.

easy.question: What did Moses take with him?
answers: Joseph’s bones
The tabernacle
The tablets of the covenant
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Moses took the bones of Joseph with him.”

easy.question: Whom had Joseph made swear an oath?
answers: Moses alone
The children of Israel
Pharaoh
easy.explanation: Joseph had made the children of Israel swear to carry up his bones.

easy.question: What did Joseph say would happen in the future?
answers: Egypt would disappear
Moses would become king
God would surely visit the Israelites
easy.explanation: Joseph said, “God will surely visit you.”

medium.question: Why did Moses take Joseph’s bones?
answers: To fulfill the oath that the Israelites had sworn
To build an altar from them
To hide them from Pharaoh
medium.explanation: Moses fulfilled Joseph’s request that the Israelites carry his bones with them.

medium.question: In the phrase “God will surely visit you,” what does “visit” mean?
answers: God will punish you
God will remember you and act on your behalf
God will count you
medium.explanation: In this context, “visit” means that God would remember the Israelites and act to save them.

medium.question: What is the order of events described in the verse?
answers: Moses took the bones, and then Joseph made the people swear
The Israelites reached the land, and then Joseph requested his bones
Joseph made the Israelites swear in the past, and Moses took the bones during the Exodus
medium.explanation: Joseph’s oath was made earlier; Moses later fulfilled it by taking Joseph’s bones.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the fact that Moses took Joseph’s bones?
answers: He honored Israel’s commitment to an earlier generation
Joseph was still alive
The bones were needed for war
challenge.explanation: Taking the bones shows that Moses and the Israelites kept the oath made to Joseph.

challenge.question: Why is Joseph’s oath mentioned in the story of the Exodus?
answers: To explain why Pharaoh released Joseph
To show that the deliverance fulfilled an earlier promise
To describe the number of Israelites
challenge.explanation: The oath connects Joseph’s hope in the past with the Exodus and the fulfillment of God’s promise.

challenge.question: What does the repeated idea in “God will surely visit you” emphasize?
answers: Uncertainty about whether God would act
That God would visit only once
Certainty that God would remember and act
challenge.explanation: The wording emphasizes confidence that God would remember the Israelites and save them.

questions.question: What can we infer from the fact that Moses took Joseph’s bones?
answers: He honored Israel’s commitment to an earlier generation
Joseph was still alive
The bones were needed for war
questions.explanation: Taking the bones shows that Moses and the Israelites kept the oath made to Joseph.

questions.question: Why is Joseph’s oath mentioned in the story of the Exodus?
answers: To explain why Pharaoh released Joseph
To show that the deliverance fulfilled an earlier promise
To describe the number of Israelites
questions.explanation: The oath connects Joseph’s hope in the past with the Exodus and the fulfillment of God’s promise.

questions.question: What does the repeated idea in “God will surely visit you” emphasize?
answers: Uncertainty about whether God would act
That God would visit only once
Certainty that God would remember and act
questions.explanation: The wording emphasizes confidence that God would remember the Israelites and save them.

paragraphs.title: The Journey from Succoth to Etham

easy.question: From which place did the Israelites set out?
answers: Succoth
Etham
The wilderness
easy.explanation: The verse says, “they took their journey from Succoth.”

easy.question: Where did they camp?
answers: Succoth
Etham
Egypt
easy.explanation: The verse says that they encamped in Etham.

easy.question: Where was Etham located?
answers: Inside the city
Beside the sea
At the edge of the wilderness
easy.explanation: The verse describes Etham as being at the edge of the wilderness.

medium.question: What was the order of events in the verse?
answers: They set out from Succoth and then camped in Etham
They camped in Etham and then left Succoth
They left the wilderness and then reached Succoth
medium.explanation: The verse first says they journeyed from Succoth and then encamped in Etham.

medium.question: What does “encamped in Etham” mean?
answers: They fought there
They stopped and set up camp there
They turned back
medium.explanation: To encamp means to stop and stay in a place as a camp.

medium.question: What can we understand about the relationship between Succoth and Etham?
answers: They were the same place
The Israelites remained in Succoth
Etham was the camping place after Succoth
medium.explanation: The verse describes traveling from Succoth and then camping in Etham, making Etham the next stop.

challenge.question: What does the movement from Succoth to Etham reveal about the journey?
answers: They were progressing toward the wilderness
They were returning to Egypt
They remained near Succoth
challenge.explanation: Since Etham was at the edge of the wilderness, the journey was progressing toward that region.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the plural verbs “they journeyed” and “they encamped”?
answers: Only one person traveled and camped
A group of people traveled and camped
The places themselves traveled and camped
challenge.explanation: The plural verbs fit a group; in this context, they refer to the Israelites.

challenge.question: What is the significance of “at the edge of the wilderness”?
answers: They were in the middle of the wilderness
They were outside every wilderness region
They were at the wilderness boundary, a place leading into it
challenge.explanation: “At the edge” indicates a border or outskirts, not the center of the wilderness.

questions.question: What does the movement from Succoth to Etham reveal about the journey?
answers: They were progressing toward the wilderness
They were returning to Egypt
They remained near Succoth
questions.explanation: Since Etham was at the edge of the wilderness, the journey was progressing toward that region.

questions.question: What can we infer from the plural verbs “they journeyed” and “they encamped”?
answers: Only one person traveled and camped
A group of people traveled and camped
The places themselves traveled and camped
questions.explanation: The plural verbs fit a group; in this context, they refer to the Israelites.

questions.question: What is the significance of “at the edge of the wilderness”?
answers: They were in the middle of the wilderness
They were outside every wilderness region
They were at the wilderness boundary, a place leading into it
questions.explanation: “At the edge” indicates a border or outskirts, not the center of the wilderness.

paragraphs.title: The Pillars of Cloud and Fire

easy.question: What went before the Israelites by day?
answers: A pillar of cloud
A pillar of fire
A pillar of water
easy.explanation: The verse says that the Lord went before them by day in a pillar of cloud.

easy.question: What did the pillar of fire do at night?
answers: It gave the people water
It gave them light
It protected their clothing
easy.explanation: The pillar of fire gave them light so they could travel at night.

easy.question: Where were the pillar of cloud and the pillar of fire in relation to the people?
answers: Behind the people
In the sea
Before the people
easy.explanation: The verse says that the pillars were before the people.

medium.question: Why was there a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night?
answers: To guide them by day and give them light by night
To feed the people
To signal only when to camp
medium.explanation: The cloud guided the way during the day, and the fire provided light at night.

medium.question: What does the statement “He took not away the pillar” mean?
answers: He did not make it shine
He did not place it there
He did not remove or abandon it
medium.explanation: The statement means that the Lord did not remove the pillars or leave the people.

medium.question: What is the order of the roles described in the verses?
answers: By day the cloud guided them, and by night the fire gave light
By night the cloud guided them, and by day the fire gave light
By day the fire gave light, and by night the cloud disappeared
medium.explanation: The verses first describe the cloud’s role by day and then the fire’s role at night.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the fact that the pillars were before the people rather than behind them?
answers: The people needed to return to Egypt
The pillars showed them the way forward
The pillars guarded only the rear of the camp
challenge.explanation: Their position before the people fits their role of guiding and leading them forward.

challenge.question: Which detail emphasizes that the Lord’s guidance was continuous?
answers: The people traveled only by day
There were two pillars at the same time
The cloud was present by day and the fire by night, and neither was removed
challenge.explanation: The change from cloud by day to fire by night, together with the statement that neither was removed, shows continual guidance.

challenge.question: What was the main difference between the pillar of cloud and the pillar of fire?
answers: The cloud guided the way, and the fire provided light
The cloud gave light, and the fire guided the way
Both served only as signals for camping
challenge.explanation: The verse assigns guidance to the cloud and illumination at night to the fire.

questions.question: What can we infer from the fact that the pillars were before the people rather than behind them?
answers: The people needed to return to Egypt
The pillars showed them the way forward
The pillars guarded only the rear of the camp
questions.explanation: Their position before the people fits their role of guiding and leading them forward.

questions.question: Which detail emphasizes that the Lord’s guidance was continuous?
answers: The people traveled only by day
There were two pillars at the same time
The cloud was present by day and the fire by night, and neither was removed
questions.explanation: The change from cloud by day to fire by night, together with the statement that neither was removed, shows continual guidance.

questions.question: What was the main difference between the pillar of cloud and the pillar of fire?
answers: The cloud guided the way, and the fire provided light
The cloud gave light, and the fire guided the way
Both served only as signals for camping
questions.explanation: The verse assigns guidance to the cloud and illumination at night to the fire.
